text: In January 2021 US Customs and Border Protection blocked a shipment of UNIQLO cotton men's shirts at the Port of Los Angeles under its ban on cotton products made with forced labour by the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (XPCC). It rejected Uniqlo's appeal because the company had not shown the shirts were made without forced labour.

source.name: Bloomberg (Lisa Du), republished by The Japan Times: U.S. blocked Uniqlo shirts over Xinjiang forced-labor concerns
source.quote: customs agency blocked a shipment of Fast Retailing Co.’s Uniqlo shirts in January for violating an order prohibiting imports of items suspected to be produced by forced labor

additionalSources.name: Sourcing Journal (WWD): Uniqlo Failed to Convince CBP its Cotton Shirts Weren’t Made with Forced Labor
additionalSources.quote: the brand failed to provide “substantial evidence” to establish that the entities within the XPCC that processed the cotton into garments “did so without the use of forced labor.”
